title.narrative: Integrated Life-Sustaining and Resilience-Based Assistance in Southern Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtThe protracted nature of the Syria crisis has undermined resilience and challenged recovery, resulting in unprecedented levels of humanitarian needs and exacerbated protection risks across the country. The number of at-risk individuals who are chronically dependent on humanitarian aid for survival is increasing each year, with 16.7 million people expected to require assistance in 2024 – the largest number since the beginning of the crisis in 2011 (HNO). Within this context, DRC is proposing a 14-month integrated, multi-sectoral programme in Busra Esh-Sham of Dar’a and Duma of Rural Damascus, where communities are grappling with the highest intersector severity of needs and prolonged socio-economic deterioration. To facilitate the provision of, and access to, essential basic services while mitigating the impact of key drivers of the crisis, DRC will implement a combination of life-sustaining and resilience-based interventions across the key sectors of Early Recovery and Livelihoods (ERL) and Shelter, expected to directly benefit approximately 881 unique individuals. DRC will ensure the centrality of protection and protection mainstreaming across all sectoral interventions, and that protection risks associated with the proposed interventions are visible and meaningfully addressed. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtUnder the ltbgtShelterlt/bgt Sector, DRC will ensure crisis-affected households have access to basic, safe, and dignified shelter and are protected from protection and other risks through the rehabilitation of 161 Partially Damaged Apartments (PDAs) in Duma and Busra Esh-Sham, benefitting approximately 805 individuals. The rehabilitation works will be implemented through a contractor modality, and special measures will be undertaken where additional protection or disability considerations are essential in promoting accessible, safe, and dignified living conditions. As shelter is fundamental to the realization of human rights and minimum standards of living, this response will reinforce an enabling and protective environment, while simultaneously seeking to increase the resilience of affected communities.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtUnder the ltbgtERLlt/bgt Sector, DRC aims to promote resilience and self-reliance among crisis-affected communities by strengthening existing Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises’ (MSMEs) technical and financial capacities to increase their income and generate employment, sustainably overtime. A total of 76 MSMEs will participate in Business Development Skills (BDS) Trainings, with a focus on foundational business management knowledge and skills that are essential for enterprises to realize their business ambitions and reach their full potential. Among whom, 54 MSMEs will also benefit from conditional cash grants to increase their financial capacities to pursue their business plans. Throughout the project, DRC will work closely with each MSME to promote maximum uptake, including tailored mentorship and coaching to ensure enterprise strategies are successful. With the current economic crisis intrinsically interlinked with basic need gaps and reliance on harmful coping strategies, improving access to decent and sustainable livelihood opportunities will be complimentary and mutually reinforcing.lt/pgt
